title: Compensation Business Partner, International
description: Why Harvey At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. Role Overview Harvey is looking for a Compensation Business Partner to ensure our compensation philosophy, principles, and practices extend to all of our markets outside of the US, initially focused on EMEA and APAC. This will be our first Compensation Business Partner dedicated to our international business sitting within the EMEA region, and an opportunity to help shape how Harvey approaches compensation as we continue to scale globally. You’ll partner closely with our People Business Partners, Recruiting team, business leaders, and the broader Compensation team to ensure our programs remain competitive, thoughtful, and scalable across markets. We’re looking for someone who combines deep compensation expertise with strong business judgment. You should be equally comfortable analyzing market data, advising a recruiter on a complex offer, partnering with a PBP and developing a point of view on how Harvey should approach compensation in a new or rapidly evolving market. This is a highly collaborative role that will have a great degree of partnership across many functions. What You'll Do Serve as the primary Compensation Business Partner for EMEA and APAC, developing deep context on our teams, talent markets, and hiring needs across the regions. Partner closely with People Business Partners and business leaders on compensation decisions including new hires, promotions, internal mobility, and other complex compensation questions. Build a particularly strong partnership with Recruiting, advising on offers, market competitiveness, and candidate-specific situations. Help evolve Harvey's international compensation strategy as we scale, including our approach to geographic differentiation, market positioning, salary structures, and equity. Bring deep equity expertise and help translate Harvey's equity philosophy across markets where candidate expectations and familiarity with US-style equity compensation can vary significantly. Research emerging compensation practices and talent trends, particularly across the rapidly evolving AI market, and turn external data into clear recommendations for Harvey. Conduct market analyses using compensation survey data and other sources, while applying judgment. Partner with the broader Compensation team on compensation cycles, benchmarking, band development, and company-wide programs, ensuring international considerations are represented from the beginning. Identify where our US practices translate internationally—and where they don't—and proactively recommend changes as Harvey enters and scales in new markets. Help build the infrastructure, principles, and enablement that will allow Harvey's international compensation approach to scale. What You Have 5-7+ years of experience in compensation Experience supporting international compensation across EMEA and/or APAC. Experience working for a US-headquartered company, with a strong understanding of how global compensation programs are designed and adapted for international markets. Meaningful experience with equity compensation, including the ability to explain and advise on equity in markets with different norms and expectations. Experience in a high-growth startup or scale-up environment; you are comfortable building while the company and market are changing around you. Strong knowledge of compensation fundamentals including market benchmarking, salary structures, job leveling, offers, promotions, retention, and pay decisions. Exceptional business partnership skills. You can build trust with leaders, PBPs, and recruiters while being willing to challenge assumptions. Strong analytical skills paired with excellent judgment—you know when the data is telling you something and when it requires additional context. Intellectual curiosity and a genuine appetite to become an expert on the AI talent market, including proactively researching competitors, compensation trends, and emerging practices. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and building new approaches rather than relying on an established playbook. Ability to communicate complicated compensation concepts simply and credibly to audiences with very different levels of compensation expertise. You'll work closely with colleagues across the business, helping to keep things on track, find better ways of doing things and make a real difference to the employee experience. Helping us stay connected: Supporting internal communications, employee updates and activities that bring our people together. Being the go-to organiser: Keeping our systems, records and processes up to date, coordinating meetings, tracking actions and helping colleagues find the information they need. Confidence communicating with employees, line managers and colleagues across different business functions. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft practical employee communications, guidance and reminders. Good digital skills and confidence using business systems, trackers and Microsoft 365 applications. Strong attention to detail and the ability to handle employee information with discretion and sound judgement. A proactive and reliable approach, with the confidence to raise gaps, delays or unclear ownership with the appropriate person. An interest in improving routine processes and making information easier for others to understand and use. The ability to balance planned People activity with defined support for wider business priorities. Desirable Experience supporting activities such as onboarding, performance reviews, employee development or engagement surveys. Familiarity with HR systems, employee platforms or maintaining reports and trackers. Experience supporting internal communications, employee events or wider business projects. Experience working in consultancy, engineering, construction or another professional services environment. A CIPD Level 3 or relevant business administration qualification. Experience creating or improving processes, guidance and templates. title: Senior Product Manager, Cruise Liners & Port Operations
description: At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors. Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success. Kpler is expanding into high-value maritime verticals, with Cruise Liners and Port Operations representing two important opportunities. Both address a common market need: the lack of independent, reliable insights into actual performance, built on observed data rather than published schedules or self-reported information. In the cruise sector, operators and analysts often rely on published itineraries rather than actual vessel movements, despite the significant fuel and carbon costs associated with fleet operations. In ports, performance data is often incomplete or self-reported, creating a need for independent benchmarking as berth-level emissions carry increasing financial implications under schemes such as the EU ETS. As a Senior Product Manager, Cruise Liners & Port Operations, you will own both products end to end, from strategy and roadmap through to the first release and go-to-market. Working closely with the Lead Product Manager – Maritime & Logistics, you will build two early-stage products in parallel, leveraging Kpler’s network of more than 13,000 AIS receivers and over 10,000 mapped ports and berths. For Cruise Liners, you will develop itinerary intelligence for tracked fleets, providing an independent view of actual sailed itineraries, fuel consumption and emissions. For Port Operations, you will build a product focused on port-level vessel activity monitoring, giving port authorities a reliable, live view of activity and performance. This is an individual-contributor role for an experienced product professional with a background in maritime, cruise, travel, ports or an adjacent B2B data/SaaS environment. You will need to balance competing priorities across two products, establish trusted data methodologies, engage customers and bring both products to market through a pragmatic, build-and-iterate approach. Key Responsibilities Own the product strategy and roadmap for Cruise Liners and Port Operations, prioritising customer needs and commercial opportunities while making trade-offs between the two products explicit. Lead market discovery with cruise operators, port authorities, harbour masters and terminal operators, gathering requirements and translating customer needs into product priorities. Drive delivery across both products, maintaining clear roadmaps, delivery cadences and launch plans, with a pragmatic approach focused on launching initial capabilities and iterating based on feedback. Establish trusted data and benchmarking methodologies for both products, developing an independent view of cruise itineraries, fuel and emissions, alongside consistent port call-cycle measurement and performance benchmarking. Collaborate with Engineering, Data, Sales, Product Marketing and other product teams to align delivery, reuse shared data and emissions capabilities, and develop early data and distribution partnerships. Define the Cruise Liners product direction, delivering fleet itinerary intelligence based on live, observed vessel movements that reflects actual sailed journeys rather than published schedules. Build the Port Operations product, providing port authorities with a reliable, live view of vessel activity using Kpler’s AIS receiver network and mapped port and berth data. Develop product positioning and competitive strategy, identifying opportunities to differentiate Kpler’s independent, first-party observed data from existing cruise analytics and port operations offerings. Drive go-to-market execution for both products, working with Product Marketing on positioning, packaging, pricing input and launch planning, and establishing repeatable customer discovery and design partnerships. Skills & Experience 6–10 years of senior product or commercial experience in maritime data, cruise or travel, ports, or an adjacent B2B data/SaaS business, with a proven track record of delivering products that customers adopt. Working fluency in at least one of cruise or port operations, with the ability to develop expertise quickly in the other. Direct experience in the cruise or ports industry, with an established network among operators, port authorities and terminals. Experience translating customer needs into product strategy and working closely with product and engineering teams to deliver solutions. Experience managing multiple products or workstreams simultaneously, balancing competing priorities and maintaining delivery momentum. Strong product discovery and roadmap prioritisation skills, with the ability to engage customers and translate market insights into actionable product requirements. Experience working with data and engineering teams to deliver data-driven products. Understanding of go-to-market planning, including product positioning, packaging and pricing input. Familiarity with maritime and trade data concepts, including AIS, port calls and voyage legs. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to engage technical and commercial teams and senior external stakeholders. A self-directed approach, with strong ownership, sound judgement and a pragmatic bias towards action. Comfort working in an ambiguous, early-stage environment, with a build-and-iterate mindset. Nice to have Experience launching a new product line or building a product from concept to market, rather than solely managing an established offering. Understanding of the regulatory environment shaping maritime and port operations, including the EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, CII and green port incentive schemes. Experience establishing customer design partnerships and building relationships with industry stakeholders to support product discovery and adoption. title: Senior Product Manager - Containers & Automotive Intelligence
description: At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors. Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success. title: Human Resource Director, Europe & Canada
description: <div class="content-intro"><p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading-[1.7]"> </p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading-[1.7]">Join New Era Technology, where People First is at the heart of everything we do. With a global team of over 3,000 professionals, we're committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued, empowered, and inspired to grow. Our mission is to securely connect people, places, and information with end-to-end technology solutions at scale.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading-[1.7]">At New Era, you'll join a team-oriented culture that prioritizes your personal and professional development. Work alongside industry-certified experts, access continuous training, and enjoy competitive benefits. Guided by our core attributes — putting people first, embracing continuous learning, and thriving through collaboration and inclusion — we nurture our people to deliver exceptional customer service.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal leading-[1.7]">If you want to make an impact in a supportive, growth-oriented environment, New Era is the place for you. Apply today and help us shape the future of work—together</p> <p> </p></div><p>The <strong>Human Resources Director, Europe & Canada</strong> is responsible for leading the HR strategy, operations, and employee experience across Canada, the United Kingdom, Belgium, and Romania. This position serves as the senior HR leader for the region and partners closely with business leaders to align people strategies with organizational priorities, business growth, and operational objectives.</p> <p>Reporting directly to the Chief Human Resources Officer in the United States, the HR Director will provide leadership across employee relations, talent acquisition, organizational design, workforce planning, talent and leadership development, succession planning, payroll oversight, employment compliance, and general HR operations.</p> <p>The successful candidate will bring strong experience operating in a complex, multi-country environment and will balance strategic leadership with effective day-to-day HR execution. The role will lead regional HR resources while collaborating closely with global HR, Talent Acquisition, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and business leadership.</p> <p>This Human Resources Director, Europe & Canada will have 3 direct reports and serves approximately 250 employees in the region. </p> <p><strong>PRIMARY DUTIES:</strong></p> <p><strong>Strategic HR Leadership & Business Partnership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the senior HR leader for Canada, the UK, Belgium, and Romania, providing strategic HR direction across the region. Other countries with small numbers of staff include France, Ireland, and the Netherlands.</li> <li>Partner with EOR vendors for employment needs in countries outside of the company’s operations.</li> <li>Partner with senior leaders and managers to translate business priorities into people strategies that drive growth, engagement, and performance.</li> <li>Use workforce data and insights to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and adapt global HR initiatives to country-specific needs.</li> </ul> <p><strong>HR Operations & Regional Leadership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead regional HR operations, ensuring consistent, scalable, and employee-focused HR practices across the employee lifecycle.</li> <li>Lead and develop the regional HR team, including HR Managers in the UK and Romania and an HR Coordinator in Romania.</li> <li>Partner with global HR to standardize and continuously improve processes while addressing local requirements.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Employee Relations</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead employee relations matters across the region, including disciplinary actions, grievances, investigations, redundancies, and dismissals.</li> <li>Coach managers to address employee relations and performance issues consistently, with appropriate documentation and escalation.</li> <li>Partner with General Counsel and external counsel on employment-related claims and proactively reduce employment risk.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Talent Acquisition & Onboarding</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own regional recruitment and onboarding of top talent in partnership with offshore recruiters and hiring managers.</li> <li>Build talent pipelines for critical roles and ensure hiring practices and documentation meet local requirements.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Talent Development, Succession & Career Planning</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead employee development, succession planning, career pathing, and leadership development across the region.</li> <li>Facilitate talent reviews with leaders to identify critical roles, high-potential employees, and capability gaps.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Payroll & HR Administration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Oversee regional payroll administration in partnership with the offshore payroll specialist team.</li> <li>Maintain strong controls and coordination between HR, Payroll, and Finance for accurate employee transactions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Employment Compliance & Risk Management</strong></p> <ul> <li>Ensure HR practices comply with employment requirements in Canada, the UK, Belgium, and Romania.</li> <li>Monitor legislative developments and recommend updates to policies, documentation, and manager practices.</li> <li>Support compliance for working time, leave, employee consultation, restructurings, redundancies, and terminations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Organizational Effectiveness & Workforce Planning</strong></p> <ul> <li>Provide guidance on organizational structure, spans of control, and workforce planning to support growth and scalability.</li> <li>Support integrations, restructurings, acquisitions, and related change and communication strategies within the region.</li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Significant progressive HR leadership experience, including experience at the HR Director, Head of HR, Senior HR Business Partner, or comparable level.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience supporting employees and leaders across multiple countries or jurisdictions.</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of employment practices and employee relations within the UK and broader European environment.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience managing complex employee relations matters, including investigations, disciplinary matters, grievances, redundancies, and dismissals.</li> <li>Experience partnering with senior business leaders on workforce planning, organizational design, restructuring, and talent strategy.</li> <li>Experience leading and developing HR professionals.</li> <li>Strong understanding of recruitment, onboarding, performance management, succession planning and employee development.</li> <li>Experience providing oversight or governance for payroll and HR operational processes.</li> <li>Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to handle confidential and sensitive employee matters.</li> <li>Excellent communication, influencing, consultation, and stakeholder-management skills.</li> <li>Ability to operate effectively within a global organization and collaborate across countries, cultures, and time zones.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred</strong></p> <ul> <li>Direct HR experience supporting employees in Canada, the United Kingdom, Belgium, and/or Romania.</li> <li>Experience within a global professional services, technology services, managed services, or similarly complex organization.</li> <li>Experience supporting acquisitions, integrations, restructurings, or other large-scale organizational transformation.</li> <li>Experience working within a global HR operating model that uses shared-services or offshore recruiting, payroll, or HR operations teams.</li> </ul> <p><strong>LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Strategic Business Partnership: </strong>Connects workforce and organizational decisions directly to business priorities and outcomes.</li> <li><strong>Commercial Acumen: </strong>Understands how talent, organizational structure, workforce costs, and leadership capability affect business performance.</li> <li><strong>Employment Risk Judgment: </strong>Balances employee experience, business objectives, consistency, and employment risk when advising leaders.</li> <li><strong>Influence & Credibility: </strong>Builds trusted relationships with senior executives, managers, employees, and global functional partners.</li> <li><strong>Change Leadership: </strong>Effectively leads organizations and employees through transformation, restructuring, integration, and growth.</li> <li><strong>Talent Mindset: </strong>Proactively develops internal talent and strengthens leadership pipelines and succession plans.</li> <li><strong>Operational Excellence: </strong>Creates consistent, scalable HR processes while recognizing when local requirements require different approaches.</li> <li><strong>Global & Cultural Awareness: </strong>Works effectively across countries and cultures and avoids applying a single-country approach to regional workforce matters.</li> <li><strong>Sound Judgment & Discretion: </strong>Demonstrates maturity and confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and legal matters.</li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>LANGUAGE SKILLS: </strong>Ability to read, understand, and interpret job-related documents, instructions, policies, and communications in English. Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, with employees, customers, vendors, and other business partners, as applicable to the position. Fluent English is required. Fluent or professional-level French language capability is preferred.</p> <p><strong>REQUIRED EDUCATION / CERTIFICATIONS: </strong>Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Preferred: CIPD or an equivalent internationally recognized HR credential.<strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>PHYSICAL DEMANDS:</strong> Regular use of hands and fingers to operate a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment, including repetitive motions such as typing, scrolling, and mouse use. Ability to communicate effectively and understand verbal communication in person, by telephone, and through video conferencing or other remote communication tools. Ability to view and read information on computer screens and printed materials, including the ability to adjust focus.

title: Senior Associate - Materials
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Company Description:</strong> Systemiq is a system-change company committed to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement by transforming markets and business models across five key systems: nature and food, materials and circularity, energy, urban areas, and sustainable finance.</p> <p>As a certified B Corp, we combine strategic advisory with high-impact, on-the-ground work, partnering with business, finance, policymakers and civil society to deliver system change. With offices across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, we are dedicated exclusively to sustainability-focused work.</p> <p></p> <p> </p></div><p></p> <h2>Strategy Associate, Materials & Circular Economy</h2> <p><strong>Location: London preferred. Amsterdam also possible</strong></p> <p>Systemiq is looking for a Strategy Associate to join our Materials & Circular Economy team. This role is suited to someone who combines strong strategic thinking with the intellectual curiosity to tackle complex sustainability challenges.</p> <p>You will work on some of the most important questions facing companies, governments and wider society as they shift towards more circular and sustainable models. Projects can range from shaping corporate strategy and identifying new business opportunities to assessing value chains, developing policy recommendations and designing system-level interventions.</p> <p>We are looking for someone who can bring the core toolkit and pace of a strong strategy consultant: structured problem-solving, analytical rigour, clear communication and sound judgement. Strategy consulting experience is one route to demonstrating this. We are equally interested in candidates from other demanding analytical environments who can show the same quality of thinking and ability to turn complexity into clear recommendations.</p> <p>You will join small, senior-led project teams and take meaningful responsibility from the outset. You will structure problems, conduct analysis, develop insights and work directly with clients to translate those insights into practical strategic choices.</p> <h3>Responsibilities</h3> <p>You will:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Structure complex problems:</strong> break ambiguous questions into clear workstreams, hypotheses and analytical priorities.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Generate insights:</strong> conduct rigorous qualitative and quantitative analysis, drawing conclusions from incomplete or complex information.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Shape recommendations:</strong> translate analysis into clear, concise and practical strategic recommendations.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Develop client materials:</strong> produce high-quality presentations, briefings and other client-ready outputs.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Engage with clients:</strong> work directly with senior stakeholders across businesses, governments, foundations and non-governmental organisations.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Contribute to project direction:</strong> help shape project approaches, hypotheses and emerging strategic conclusions.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Build trusted relationships:</strong> work effectively with clients, partners and stakeholders across multi-organisation initiatives.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>About the team</h3> <p>You will be part of Systemiq's Materials & Circular Economy platform, led by Partner Ben Dixon.</p> <p>Ben works across circular economy and energy topics and has advised organisations including the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, the United Nations International Resource Panel and multinational companies across packaging, chemicals and related sectors. He also leads Systemiq's work on plastics, focused on accelerating the transition towards a more circular and resource-efficient plastics system.</p> <h3>What we are looking for</h3> <h4>Strategy and analytical capability</h4> <p>We are looking for candidates who already demonstrate, or can quickly operate with, the core toolkit expected in strategy consulting. You should be able to:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Structure complex and ambiguous problems into clear components, hypotheses and analytical questions.</p> </li> <li> <p>Apply strong analytical judgement to qualitative and quantitative information.</p> </li> <li> <p>Synthesize complex material into concise insights and decision-relevant recommendations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Communicate clearly in writing and verbally, including through high-quality presentation materials.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work effectively at pace, managing changing priorities and imperfect information.</p> </li> <li> <p>Move comfortably between detailed analysis and the broader strategic question.</p> </li> </ul> <h4>Experience and background</h4> <p>You will typically bring:</p> <ul> <li> <p>At least two years of experience in strategy consulting, advisory or another analytically demanding environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Evidence of strong performance and increasing responsibility in your previous roles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience contributing to strategy, investment, commercial or other decision-focused work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong academic achievement, typically including a Master's degree or equivalent experience.</p> </li> </ul> <p>We particularly welcome candidates from strategy consulting, but relevant experience could also come from corporate strategy, investing, high-growth businesses, specialist advisory firms or other project-based environments where structured thinking and analytical rigour are central to the role.</p> <h4>Sector interest and understanding</h4> <p>You do not need to be a specialist across every part of the Materials & Circular Economy agenda. You should, however, bring:</p> <ul> <li> <p>An understanding of, or demonstrated ability to learn, complex industrial and consumer value chains.</p> </li> <li> <p>Exposure to sectors such as plastics, petrochemicals, chemicals, consumer goods, manufacturing, mobility, energy or waste management.</p> </li> <li> <p>A strong interest in sustainability, circular economy and the economic and strategic questions involved in system change.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Location</h3> <p>London is the preferred location for this role. We would also consider Amsterdam for candidates whose experience and capabilities are an especially strong match for the position.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><div id="description__body"></div> <p><strong data-start="578" data-end="603">Diversity & Inclusion</strong><br data-start="603" data-end="606">At Systemiq, we absolutely believe diverse perspectives are essential to driving system change. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel respected, supported and able to do their best work.</p> <p>Click <a href="https://www.systemiq.earth/privacy-policy/">here</a> to view our Data Policy.</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Software Engineer
description: <h3><strong>Senior Engineer</strong></h3> <p>Location: Bristol, London or Edinburgh (hybrid, three days a week in the office)</p> <p>Level: Senior Engineer II (TL1)</p> <p>Team: Engineering</p> <p>Contract: Permanent</p> <p>Reporting To: Software Engineering Manager</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>About Kaluza</strong></p> <p>Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.</p> <p> </p> <p>Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.</p> <p> </p> <p>With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <p>You’ll join a technology community of product-focused and data-led product and platform engineers working at scale. We have a diverse ecosystem, spanning TypeScript on AWS, Go on GCP and Scala, we index on product-minded problem solving over language purity.</p> <p>As a Senior Engineer you’ll own a slice of the product end-to-end, from design through to production, and you’ll build AI coding agents as your default. We’re looking for someone whose judgement is worth more than their typing speed.</p> <p>From your first day you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and access to the systems you need through MCP. Our tools and conventions evolve quickly, and you’ll directly impact how we build from here.</p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Own a slice of the product end to end: </strong>shape the problem with product and design, build the interface and the services behind it, ship it, and run it in production.</li> <li><strong>Work across the stack over time</strong>: depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.</li> <li><strong>Build with AI coding agents as your default</strong>: Break work down so agents can execute, direct them, and review their output as carefully as you’d review a colleague’s pull request. You’ll also maintain the tests and safeguards that let agent written code merge safely.</li> <li><strong>Stay close to the people who use what you build: </strong>directly or through our forward-deployed engineers: a supplier’s operations team, a customer plugging in a car at night. Instrument what you ship so you can see how it’s used, and turn what you learn into shipped changes.</li> <li><strong>Make good work the default: </strong>shape the codebase, conventions and automated checks so that agents and new teammates produce the right thing without anyone catching it in review.</li> <li><strong>Mentor the team around you:</strong> Coach and mentor your peers and help improve how we work and evolve as a team. </li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></p> <p> </p> <p>These are the practices and behaviours we see most in our top engineers and value deeply, but we don't expect everyone to tick every single box. If you're excited by the role and can see yourself thriving here, we’d love to hear from you.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Experience shipping production software:</strong> You have a depth of experience in either a front-end or back-end of a modern stack, and potentially an openness to stretch across both as you navigate our diverse ecosystem.</li> <li><strong>AI coding tools:</strong> You build with tools like Cursor or Claude Code, can walk us through work you’ve shipped this way and review AI output as rigorously as a colleague’s pull request.</li> <li><strong>Able to navigate a complex, high-stakes domain:</strong> You keep complex energy logic legible across microservices, knowing exactly when to use sync vs async to prevent cascading failures.</li> <li><strong>Cloud and operational ownership:</strong> You're comfortable deploying on major cloud platforms using shared tooling. You fully own your software in production, which includes participating in an out-of-hours on-call rota.</li> <li><strong>Strong product sense.</strong> You ask the “why” before building, and you can describe a time when user feedback or metrics changed what you shipped.</li> <li><strong>Clear written communication.</strong> You write specs, pull request descriptions and post-mortems with enough clarity and context that either a human teammate or an AI agent can immediately act on them.</li> <li><strong>A multiplier for your team:</strong> You mentor peers and proactively shape how the team works; introducing conventions, checks or shared context that makes everyone else’s output consistently better.</li> </ul> <p><strong>It would be great if you have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience building tooling around coding agents, such as MCP servers, skills or CI checks</li> <li>Experience in energy, or another real-time or regulated field</li> </ul> <p><strong>Our Values</strong></p> <p>Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:</p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Play to win:</strong> Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.</li> <li><strong>Solve the real problem:</strong> Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.</li> <li><strong>Build trust every day:</strong> Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.</li> <li><strong>Own the outcome:</strong> Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.</li> <li><strong>Go further together: </strong>Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Our Perks</strong></p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Time off and family:</strong> 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period</li> <li><strong>Health and security:</strong> Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests</li> <li><strong>Pay and flexibility:</strong> Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% of salary to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work</li> <li><strong>Growth and setup:</strong> Personal learning budget, home office budget</li> <li><strong>Climate:</strong> Access to Furthr, our climate action app</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Come as you are</strong></p> <p> </p> <p>We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.</p> <p> </p> <p>This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.</p> <p> </p> <p>Find out more on our<a href="https://www.kaluza.com/careers/"> careers page</a> and<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/kaluza/"> LinkedIn</a>. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is<a href="https://www.kaluza.com/applicant-data-protection-notice/"> here</a>.</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Talent Acquisition Coordinator
description: Let’s transform banking forever ClearBank is built on the belief that banking infrastructure shouldn’t slow down progress. Quite the opposite. Speed it up and that’s when you unlock potential. When you really start to innovate. That spirit and ‘can-do’ attitude is why our clients – from FinTech's and crypto platforms, to banks and credit unions – choose to use our API to power their banking infrastructure. But it’s our people who are the stars here. They power that innovation, push harder to break boundaries. They make coming to work (or working from home) fun. They’re the ones we trust to catapult our clients to success. Just as they trust us to build a business that’s always striding forward. What you can expect: As our Talent Acquisition Coordinator, you’ll play an important role in creating a seamless and welcoming experience for candidates and keeping our Talent Acquisition operations running smoothly. You’ll coordinate interviews, maintain accurate information in Ashby and support the production of regular Talent Acquisition reporting. You’ll also work with colleagues across Talent to support supplier administration and help organise our monthly induction for new joiners. This role is suited to someone who enjoys bringing structure to a busy environment, cares about getting the details right and wants every interaction with ClearBank to leave a positive impression. Your role includes: Complete the day-to-day administration of Ashby, maintaining accurate and complete candidate, vacancy and recruitment information to support reliable reporting and compliant hiring processes. Coordinate interviews across multiple time zones, managing candidate and interviewer communication and availability to create a timely, organised and professional experience. Welcome and support candidates attending interviews at the ClearBank office, particularly senior candidates, creating a positive and professional first impression. Monitor recruitment activity and data quality in Ashby, identifying missing, inaccurate or outdated information and working with recruiters to resolve issues promptly. Produce accurate weekly Talent Acquisition dashboards and insights, providing clear visibility of recruitment activity and data to the Talent Acquisition Lead. Support wider Talent operations, including supplier onboarding and offboarding for the Head of Talent and the organisation of monthly new-joiner induction with the Talent Development Manager. Identify opportunities to improve Talent Acquisition coordination and administration, suggesting practical ways to make processes simpler, clearer and more effective. What does success in this role look like: Ashby contains accurate, complete and dependable recruitment information that the Talent Acquisition team can confidently use for reporting and decision-making. Candidates experience organised, timely and thoughtful communication throughout interview coordination and when visiting the ClearBank office. Interviews are coordinated effectively across stakeholders and time zones, with scheduling problems identified and resolved promptly. Weekly Talent Acquisition dashboards are produced accurately and consistently, giving the Talent Acquisition Lead clear visibility of recruitment activity. Supplier administration and monthly induction coordination are organised and reliable, with the relevant stakeholders kept informed. What you’ll bring: To excel in this role, you’ll also need: Previous experience in a Talent Acquisition, recruitment coordination or similar role, with hands-on experience supporting interview scheduling, candidate administration and day-to-day recruitment processes. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple interviews, activities and competing priorities. Excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with recruitment systems, schedules, reports and confidential information. Confidence communicating with candidates and colleagues at different levels of seniority. The ability to use digital systems effectively and learn new technology and processes quickly. A methodical approach to maintaining accurate records and identifying missing or inconsistent information. The ability to take ownership of assigned tasks, follow agreed processes and ask for support when needed. A little bit more about us! ClearBank is Where You Can belong: At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 42% of our senior management roles are held by women Our enhanced family leave policies Launching our partnership with Code First Girls Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group Our hiring process and what you can expect: Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team. Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! Our commitment to you as a candidate: We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon! Equal Opportunities ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. The legal bit By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy
description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. About the role The Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy will lead Checkout’s external-facing compliance strategy across banking, scheme and other strategic partner relationships. You will own the operating model and delivery of compliance-related partner engagements, including annual reviews, periodic due diligence, requests for information, licensing and scheme initiatives, and readiness for product or geographic expansion. You will ensure that Checkout presents a consistent, accurate and well-evidenced view of its compliance framework, while converting external expectations into practical improvements to our roadmap, controls, processes and operating model. The role combines strategic ownership, senior stakeholder management and hands-on delivery. You will lead complex engagements, advise Compliance leadership, build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and develop the partner-engagement capability of the team, including managing and coaching Senior Analyst(s) as the structure is established. What you will do Own the Compliance Strategy partner-engagement portfolio, prioritising work across banking partners, schemes and other strategic external stakeholders. Establish and continuously improve the operating model for partner engagements, including governance, roles and responsibilities, service standards, evidence expectations, response libraries, escalation routes and management information. Lead annual KYC AML partner compliance reviews, partner onboarding or refreshes, complex RFIs and other material external engagements from planning through to closure. Act as a senior Compliance representative in partner meetings, with high level input around Checkout’s compliance framework, risk management approach, policies, controls, governance and improvement plans with clarity and confidence. Provide oversight and challenge to response packs, control narratives, policy summaries, presentations and supporting evidence, ensuring consistency, accuracy and appropriate ownership. Lead compliance support for scheme, product-launch and geographic-expansion initiatives, ensuring external partner obligations and readiness requirements are identified, tracked and addressed. Translate partner feedback, requests and emerging expectations into strategic recommendations, roadmap priorities, control enhancements and process improvements. Build strong working relationships across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product, Operations, Commercial, Finance, Technology and regional teams to align delivery and resolve dependencies. Maintain clear governance over engagement risks, issues, decisions, action plans and remediation, escalating material matters to the Head of Compliance Strategy and relevant governance forums. Produce concise and decision-useful updates for Compliance leadership, senior management and governance committees, including themes, trends, risks, commitments and delivery status. Partner with relevant second-line teams to ensure external engagement activity is consistent with the Compliance framework, risk appetite, regulatory obligations and the responsibilities of the three lines of defence. Coach, develop and set clear expectations for Senior Analyst(s). Create and implement a high-quality, scalable and collaborative partner-engagement framework. Identify opportunities to use better data, tooling, workflow design and documentation to improve response quality, reduce duplication and increase the resilience of the Compliance operating model. Represent Compliance Strategy in cross-functional strategic initiatives and take on other priorities that support long-term capability maturation. What you will need to be successful Typically 3–5 years of experience in a similar role within compliance, regulatory compliance, risk, audit, legal or a related function in payments, fintech, banking or another regulated financial-services environment. Demonstrable experience leading external partner, banking, scheme, audit, regulatory or due-diligence engagements. Experience translating regulatory or partner expectations into practical requirements, delivery plans, governance and measurable improvements. Experience leading complex, cross-functional workstreams with multiple stakeholders, dependencies and deadlines. Experience coaching or managing people, setting priorities, giving feedback and creating clarity in a fast-moving environment. Strong understanding of the payments ecosystem and the compliance expectations relevant to banking partners, payment schemes and regulated financial institutions. Working knowledge of relevant compliance domains such as AML/CTF, sanctions, KYC/CDD/EDD, licensing, safeguarding, operational resilience, regulatory change or control assurance. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present complex issues, defend recommendations and influence senior stakeholders. Strong judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively, distinguish material from non-material issues and escalate appropriately. Strong organisational, analytical and project-management skills, with a track record of delivering high-quality outcomes under pressure. ICA, ACAMS or another relevant professional qualification is desirable. How you will work at Checkout Be The Owner: Set direction, create accountability and ensure commitments are delivered. Talk Straight: Give clear, evidence-led advice and communicate difficult messages respectfully and early. One Team: Build alignment across functions and regions, sharing context and bringing people with you. No Room for Approximation: Set a high bar for accuracy, evidence, consistency and regulatory defensibility. Athlete Mindset: Plan rigorously, raise the standard and keep improving the capability of the function. Better Every Day: Turn recurring engagement friction into scalable processes, tools and operating-model improvements. Pace Matters: Balance urgency with thoughtful risk judgement and disciplined execution. Fundamentally Positive: Lead with trust, humility and a practical, solution-oriented approach. What success looks like Partner engagement framework is clearly documented with detailed SLAs and communicated to all relevant stakeholders. Partner engagements are planned, governed and delivered consistently across the portfolio. Checkout is represented externally through clear, accurate, credible and coherent compliance narratives. Material risks, gaps and commitments are visible to the right stakeholders and managed through to resolution. Scheme, product and geographic-expansion initiatives receive timely and practical Compliance Strategy support. Partner feedback is converted into measurable improvements in processes, documentation, monitoring, tooling and capability. The Senior Analyst(s) and wider stakeholder network have clear priorities, effective ways of working and opportunities to grow. Compliance leadership has reliable management information to understand engagement themes, risks, capacity and progress. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us. For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com , follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Europe Strategy & Operations Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>About Faire</strong></span></p> <p>Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.</p> <p>We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.</p></div><p class="p1"><strong>About this role</strong></p> <p class="p1">We're looking for a strategic, analytical leader to drive growth and performance across our European and International business. In this role you'll personally own a high-impact portfolio of initiatives, doing the deep analytical work and driving execution yourself, while setting strategic direction and coaching a small team of individual contributors.</p> <p class="p1">You’ll connect the dots across product and go-to-market, using analytics, customer insights, and opportunity sizing to decide where we invest and how we execute. You’ll partner closely with Product, Operations, Revenue, and Data Science, and become a trusted advisor to senior leadership across the business.</p> <p class="p1">This is a player-coach role for someone who wants to shape strategy and also roll up their sleeves to deliver results. This role is based in London.</p> <p class="p1"><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Drive OKR attainment for the International team, owning strategy and execution for our Europe Top 8 priorities</li> <li class="li1">Lead and develop a team of Strategy & Operations ICs through coaching, prioritization, and vision setting</li> <li class="li1">Personally own key initiatives in Europe: identify opportunities that move company metrics, align cross-functional teams, remove roadblocks, and lead execution end to end</li> <li class="li1">Prioritize GTM and Product initiatives based on impact, strategic importance, and complexity, and partner with Data Science to build and refine the models that support those decisions</li> <li class="li1">Proactively identify opportunities that grow retailer lifetime value (LTV)</li> <li class="li1">Drive forecasting, performance monitoring, and metric decomps, and surface the insights that matter most to leadership</li> <li class="li1">Build effective, scalable operational processes and close operational gaps</li> <li class="li1">Build trusted relationships with key stakeholders across Product, Operations, Revenue, and leadership</li> </ul> <p class="p1"><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">8+ years of experience in consulting, finance (investment banking or private equity), or analytical business operations roles</li> <li class="li1">Experience managing and developing people</li> <li class="li1">Some experience partnering with GTM and Product teams</li> <li class="li1">You are an exceptional creative problem solver. You can break down ambiguous problems and structure a path to an answer.</li> <li class="li1">You are analytical and comfortable with data. You have strong analytical thinking and SQL knowledge, or the willingness to learn it quickly.</li> <li class="li1">You have strong product and business intuition. You can place insights in the context of broader business goals.</li> <li class="li1">You are a scrappy, resourceful executor. When something needs to get done, you remove roadblocks and find a way to make it happen.</li> <li class="li1">You are highly collaborative and influence effectively through others</li> <li class="li1">You are a clear, structured communicator, both written and verbal</li> <li class="li1">You have a strong work ethic and an ownership mindset, and you stay calm and perform under pressure and tight deadlines</li> <li class="li1">You embrace the adventure and do whatever it takes to ensure success</li> </ul> <p><strong>Salary Range</strong></p> <p>London: the pay range for this role is £141,000 to £193,500 per year. </p> <p>This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;"><em data-stringify-type="italic">Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday).</em> Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. <br></span></em></p> <p><strong>Why you’ll love working at Faire</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Move fast:</strong> You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.</li> <li><strong>Equipped to scale:</strong> We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.</li> <li><strong>Best in class:</strong> Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.</li> <li><strong>Real rewards.</strong> Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.</li> <li><strong>Belonging:</strong> We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.</li> </ul> <p>Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. To learn more about Faire and our customers, you can read more on our <a href="https://blog.faire.com/">blog</a>.</p> <p></p> <p>Faire provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression.</p> <p>Faire is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and applicants with a disability may request to be accommodated throughout the recruitment process. We will work with all applicants to accommodate their individual accessibility needs.  To request reasonable accommodation, please fill out our <a href="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSczpI9me7nYKhunSC6AlagHKv75LHqfi-Qi2TP_3dpin0Uc9Q/viewform">Accommodation Request Form</a> (<a href="https://bit.ly/faire-form)">https://bit.ly/faire-form)</a></p> <p><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Privacy</strong></p> <p>For information about the type of personal data Faire collects from applicants, as well as your choices regarding the data collected about you, please visit Faire’s <a class="c-link" href="https://www.faire.com/privacy" target="_blank" data-stringify-link="https://www.faire.com/privacy" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Privacy Notice (https://www.faire.com/privacy)</a></p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Sales Executive (Perform by Marcus Evans)
description: Marcus Evans is a global leader in business intelligence, helping our clients grow by making connections, sharing knowledge, inspiring people, building relationships and creating new opportunities. Since 1983, we have brought decision-makers together through high-level summits, conferences, online platforms and performance programmes, working across all sectors and regions. Our overriding approach is one of collaboration, and our belief that “We’ll be our most successful when we work together.” We recognise excellence and actively develop top performers into future leaders. Our culture promotes teamwork, continuous learning and global career growth. About Perform Perform by Marcus Evans is our performance-improvement consultancy. We don’t sell off-the-shelf training. We start with a diagnosis of what is actually holding a team or an organisation back, prescribe the programme that fixes it, deliver bespoke learning pathways facilitated by vetted trainers/coaches, and then assess what changed. Clients get a written view of the gaps, the fix and the result. Job Summary We are hiring a Senior Sales Executives to sell Perform to senior leaders at large organisations: Heads of HR, L&D, Talent and Transformation, and the business executives who sponsor their programmes. You will own the sale from first conversation to signed contract, working with our Programme Scientist, who builds the diagnosis and prescription behind every proposal. This is a consultative sale with long cycles, several stakeholders and meaningful deal values. We are looking for someone who has done it before and wants to build a book of business from the start. This is an onsite role based in our London office. Key Responsibilities Generate and qualify your own pipeline through targeted outreach, networking, referrals and social selling to senior HR, L&D and business leaders Run structured discovery calls using our Initial Discovery Template, so the client’s real performance problem is clear before any proposal is written Work with the Programme Scientist to turn discovery into a bespoke diagnosis, prescription and quote, and present it to the client sponsor Position Perform as an expert advisor, qualify prospects rigorously, and manage intake so each quarter’s cohorts are full and the programme stays selective Negotiate pricing and terms within our pricing framework, and take contracts through to signature Keep every opportunity current in HubSpot CRM, from contact to lead to deal, so forecasting and reporting are accurate Stay with the client after signature through delivery and assessment, and use the findings to open expansion and renewal conversations Share what you learn from the market (objections, competitors, pricing pressure) with the leadership team so the offer keeps improving Qualifications Required: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Behavioural Science or related fields. At least five years of B2B sales experience, including closing complex, high-value deals with multiple stakeholders Proven experience selling leadership development, learning and development, coaching, talent, HR consulting or other professional services to senior buyers A record of meeting or exceeding targets, with examples you can discuss Excellent written and spoken English, and the credibility to hold a conversation with a C-suite executive Comfort with discovery-led, consultative selling rather than product pitching Right to work in the UK Preferred: Experience selling to financial services, banking, technology or other regulated, multinational clients An existing network among HR and L&D decision-makers Experience working alongside subject-matter experts or consultants to build proposals HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator or comparable CRM and prospecting tools Additional languages Marcus Evans is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity, and all employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit and business need. #LI-Onsite Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Management Director – Soft FM & Estates (UK)
description: About SINGU At SINGU , we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business. Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide , supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started. Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus. If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation. About the Role You'll own a significant slice of the SINGU product suite: space management and Soft FM services – cleaning standards, portering, and catering – used every day primarily across the UK healthcare market . Product-market fit is established and thousands of users depend on these products daily. What the portfolio needs now is strategic direction and taking them to their next level of growth. You'll do that through a team of four Product Managers who are domain experts in the products they run. This is a hands-on leadership role . You'll stay close to customer problems yourself, you'll raise the bar on how the team discovers and validates work, and you'll have real autonomy to decide what's worth building – and to prove it works. SINGU group grows both organically and through acquisition, and several of these products arrived with the companies that built them. You'll shape the strategy for bringing them into one coherent ecosystem and lead your team through that change. If you enjoy taking a set of good but separate products and making them add up to something bigger, that is the interesting part of this job. You'll partner closely with Sales, Engineering, and Product colleagues across the SINGU Group so your portfolio drives revenue and solves real problems across the European FM market. AI is a must-have lever in our industry rather than a talking point: you'll be applying it where it measurably improves how our customers run their estates. This is a remote position with periodic travel to London and Kraków – roughly every two to four weeks. Role Scope People Leadership & Team Development: Manage and develop the Product Managers within the product team. Own the full management lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, feedback, coaching, performance evaluations, promotions, and exits . Foster a high-performing product culture based on customer empathy, data-driven decision-making, and outcome orientation. Manage staffing and focus areas across the suite, reallocating product resources where needed to balance discovery workload and meet strategic priorities. Lead the team through change – new ways of working, a shifting portfolio, and product consolidation – bringing people with you rather than around them. Product Discovery & Strategy: Define and maintain product roadmaps aligned with business objectives, customer needs, and market trends. Decide where to invest and where to hold : set a clear, defensible position on which initiatives scale and communicate it across the business. Build strong alignment with the Sales team to ensure product discovery and roadmap priorities actively unblock deals and support revenue growth. Identify and resolve ambiguities, dependencies, and competing priorities that impact discovery quality and speed. Product Management Best Practices & Standards: Promote modern product practices, including continuous discovery, outcome-based roadmapping, and hypothesis-driven development . description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About AlphaSense: </strong></h2> <p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit <span><a href="http://www.alpha-sense.com" target="_blank">www.alpha-sense.com</a></span>. Come join us.</span></p></div><p><strong>About Expert Insights:</strong><br>Expert Insights, which spans AlphaSense’s Expert Transcript Library and 1x1 Call Services offerings,<span class="Apple-converted-space">  </span>delivers a new and transformative form of market intelligence content.
